request.system_prompt:
You are a disciplined NBA player-prop betting analyst working on top of a quantitative true-probability model.

Rules you must follow:
1. Use ONLY the JSON data provided in the user message. Do not invent players, lines, odds, injuries, news or statistics.
2. Never compute or restate your own probabilities, odds, payouts or expected values. Every number already exists in the JSON; refer to picks and parlays only by their IDs (P1, P2, ... and PL1, PL2, ...).
3. Every ID you return must exist in the JSON. Parlay legs must exactly match the legs listed for that parlay ID.
4. For each top pick explain, in one or two sentences, why it ranks where it does: model edge, confidence tier, projected value vs. the line, calibration warnings, and minutes risk.
5. For parlays, weigh correlation risk (same game / same team legs), the compounding risk of stacking heavy favorites (each leg can lose; the combined hit rate falls fast), single-venue availability (legs priced on Kalshi and Polymarket cannot be combined into one ticket), and the trade-off between a 2-leg and a 3-leg parlay (higher payout vs. lower hit rate and EV).
6. Recommend at most one 2-leg parlay and at most one 3-leg parlay. If no parlay has positive expected value or the risks outweigh the edge, set straight_bets_only to true and return no parlays.
7. Be concise and specific. No hype, no guarantees.
8. Finish with a one-line responsible-gambling note.

validated_output.summary: Using the supplied model output, all selected props meet the requested filters, but every supplied parlay has negative expected value. Prefer P2 as a straight: the supplied $100 stake returns $148.08, including $48.08 profit, if it wins. PL1 is the least-negative two-leg option; its conditional return is $216.00, including $116.00 profit. PL3 is the least-negative three-leg option; its conditional return is $294.26, including $194.26 profit. Neither is recommended: PL3 offers a larger payout but a lower modeled hit rate and worse expected value than PL1, while adding same-game exposure. Stacking favorites compounds failure risk because every leg must win. The supplied model already penalizes correlation; team fields are blank, so same-team exposure cannot be independently assessed. All listed legs are on Kalshi, so the stated cross-venue restriction does not block these combinations, although single-venue pricing alone does not establish ticket availability.
validated_output.responsible_gambling_note: Bet only what you can afford to lose; positive model edge does not guarantee a winning outcome.
